Posted February 19, 2001
(MarijuanaNews note: I think that the AMMA’s effort to recall California District Attorneys who refuse to uphold state law – specifically Proposition 215 – is an enormously important development. They are getting more and more support.)
See
Why Patients Are Demanding Recall Elections - by Steve Kubby, AMMA Director

AMMA RECALL COMMITTEE

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:
2/19/00

CONTACT:
Jay R. Cavanaugh, Ph.D (818) 346-4493
Recall Committee Chair and Medical Advisory Board, AMMA

NOTE:

This Statement of Purpose is being sent to all California District Attorneys, putting them on legal notice to stop violating the law and the rights of sick, disabled and dying patients.

AMMA RECALL COMMITTEE - Statement of Purpose

We the collective participants in the AMMA, friends, family, educators, and treating Professionals declare that:

1. A clear and present Public Health Danger exists in the State of California where sick, disabled, and dying patients are denied their right to receive unhindered access to adjunctive therapy with Medical Cannabis as provided for in the California Constitution as of the 1996 passage of Proposition 215.

2. A majority of State and local law enforcement agencies continue to treat the use, possession, or cultivation of Medical Cannabis as a crime. Prosecutions continue throughout the State with the exception of some extraordinary jurisdictions where reasonable local guidelines have been adopted.

3. Taxpayers are financing expensive police investigations, illegal arrests, asset seizures, prosecutions, show trials, and incarceration of patients in direct defiance of California Law. Citizens are further, incurring the large and unacceptable liabilities of such actions including the real pain and suffering of patients. Continuing such policies and practices is a direct violation of Civil Rights and may constitute a continuing criminal enterprise subject to severe sanctions. Class action suits are anticipated and numerous Civil suits have already been filed.

4. The Governor of the State of California, Gray Davis, the Attorney General, William Lockyer, and the California State Legislature, have failed for four years to implement the stated will of the people. Guidance from the Courts has been lacking leaving individual Judges to fend for themselves. District Attorney who disagree with the Compassionate Use Act have been allowed to arrest patients resulting in imprisonment, inappropriate diversion to Drug Treatment, expensive show trials, and punitive plea bargains forced on sick defendants to escape death while incarcerated.

5. The State Attorney General and a large number of District Attorney¹s are in violation of their fiduciary responsibilities under the law. Oversight has failed to materialize giving de facto sanction to the adoption of repressive policies in violation of the Brown Act.

THEREFORE WE DECLARE THAT:

District Attorney¹s throughout the State are sincerely and seriously advised to reach legal accommodations such as the Oakland City Guidelines. Reasonable guidelines focusing on patient health and adopted in Public by local authorities in conjunction with local physicians, caregivers, and patients are vital in restoring reason to chaos and changing indifference to compassion. The critical healing relationship between Physician and Patient must be protected.

Officials having been given Notice through this Communication, Jury Acquittals, Court Decisions, and the standing Law of the State of California, shall be held accountable to the Electorate from whom their power is derived. Recall of District Attorney¹s and other local and State Officers shall be pursued where necessary.

All legal sanctions directed at legitimate Medical Cannabis patients in violation of the Compassionate Use Act must be halted by written and published order, immediately. Inclusive and public local task forces to adopt reasonable medical guidelines in accord with Proposition 215 should be declared, and training provided to local police and sheriff¹s to insure patient rights. Participation of local Medical and Pharmaceutical Society’s in addition to State Licensing Boards is strongly encouraged.

Violations of Proposition 215 rights under Color of Authority must be identified and prosecuted with the same vigor as the sanctions against other criminal acts. Such violations include but are not limited to arbitrary arrests of patients and caregivers, and the intimidation of Physicians.

February 2001
From Tax Talk Bulletin

The 1,200 member League of Placer County Taxpayers is one of the most influential organizations in Placer County.

WAR ON DRUGS -- in Sacramento!

For the past two years a Special Operations Drug Unit of Placer County Sheriff Edward Bonner’s department has been conducting operations, as many as 30 of them, in Sacramento County.
See
Even In The State Capital, California Narks Violate Prop 215 and the Attorney General Won’t Do His Duty.

The recent outcome of this activity has resulted in a handful of civil lawsuits against Placer County claiming unwarranted searches and violation of constitutional rights of individuals whose homes were raided.

The subjects of the drug raids were accused of cultivating and using marijuana despite the Medical Marijuana Act (Prop. 215) enacted by California and Placer County voters in 1996.

What is going on here and why are Placer County agents working in Sacramento? The interests here are why are Placer taxpayers subsidizing police work in another county, using our jails to house and feed arrestees, and prosecuting cases at county expense for another jurisdiction? Also, under Proposition 215 persons with a doctor’s approval or prescription may possess and use marijuana for treatment of health conditions they may have. Federal law does not permit distribution of marijuana.

Were sheriff agents breaking one law (215) in order to enforce the federal law?
See
California Constitution Specifically Prohibits State Officials From Using Federal Laws As An Excuse For Not Enforcing State Laws Like Prop 215 Without A Court Ruling. Great Orange County Register Editorial.

The taxpayers’ interest in this matter is the liability judgments that may arise from these lawsuits. The county is self-insured for $1million with an insurance umbrella above that amount. But each lawsuit pertains to a first million. It’s not cumulative.
See
Placer County Ignores Risks Posed By Violence-Prone Sheriff Searching For Marijuana – Will It Be First County Bankrupted By Negligent Handling Of Prop 215? Exclusive to MarijuanaNews.com

The Medical Marijuana Act (215) did not specify any prescribed amount of marijuana or plant cultivation limits. See
What Part Of 'Exempt' Do California District Attorneys Still Not Understand?

Some counties and cities have determined and publicized the amounts they accept under 215. Nevada County allows 10 plants. Sierra County permits 6 indoor plants and 3 outdoor plants. City of Oakland approves of 148 plants. There is no general agreement on an acceptable number, but if counties set and publicize the medically acceptable number of plants, or pounds, that an individual may have, then at least medical marijuana users will know when they will be free of unreasonable searches and arrest. Such an agreement will have no legal basis since 215 set no such number, but this arrangement would provide a temporary issue settlement until the state legislature provides an answer.

Last year a legislative bill by John Vasconcellos to establish a program to register medical marijuana users and provide them with an identity card such as handicapped persons now have available. The program was voluntary, but it died in committee and for good reason. No citizen desires to give public notice of an illness they may have and no one is ready to sign up that they may be in violation of the federal law regarding marijuana use.
See
Drug Czar’s Statement On California SB 848 Is Finally Online –
Maybe They Just Sobered Up After The Alcohol Lobby’s Parties.

One Placer Drug Unit raid occurred in Roseville at the home of Lyman Sanborn and his wife, Grace, that they share with their mature son. Mr. Sanborn was childhood chum of President Ronald Reagan. No evidence of any marijuana was found at the home. This was also the case in several of the other drug raids. Most medical marijuana users grow their own plants indoors. The Sanborns have filed a one million lawsuit against Placer County.

The drug squad had been observing patrons of a nursery shop in Sacramento called Green Fire. The store specializes in materials for hydroponics and culture of orchids and other exotic plants. The younger Sanborn was observed attending the Green Fire store and the drug squad traced the residence through Department of Motor Vehicles registration. Also, the Sanborn utility energy use records were obtained to verify higher than normal electric use, possibly for marijuana plant cultivation. It appears that a federal narcotics agent, Richard Adams, of the IRS Criminal Investigation Division, assisted with a federal subpoena to obtain the electric power data. So, apparently the federal drug agency was working with Placer detectives.
See
Placer County Sheriff Raids Wrong Home, Terrorizes Elderly Couple.
And, Oh Yes, Seeks More Money For Marijuana Eradication.
We Couldn’t Make This Up. -- 2 Articles

Recently a medical marijuana case in neighboring El Dorado County ended with a jury acquittal of the defendants, the Whitakers. Apparently their run-in with El Dorado officials was because that sheriff considered the Whitakers 4.2 pounds of marijuana was more than necessary for personal use and that they were probably selling it. This, generally, is the basis for drug enforcement activities of Placer and Sacramento Counties as well. At the Whitaker trial, it was noted that an on-going federal government study allows patients 6.5 pounds of the drug per year.

The League interviewed Placer District Attorney Bradford Fenocchio and Sheriff Edward Bonner regarding Placer County¹s drug activities. Bonner indicated that he and Sacramento deputy DA, Dale Kitching, had originally engaged in a mutual aid pact but that Sacramento did not follow through due to other commitments. Bonner indicated that his drug unit in no longer working outside the county.

The League suggested that Mr. Fenocchio work with other law enforcement units in Placer and establish a medical marijuana use amount that would not be subject to house raids, and to publish the same. Fenocchio indicated that he was already exploring this avenue and that some agreed upon amount would be established in a few months. Fenocchio also agreed and indicated that he would continue to consult with State Attorney General Lockyer and the legislature to come up with a more formal response. The League suggested that the DA and the sheriff’s department should reconsider their aggressive medical marijuana program.

For those readers that are skeptical of medical marijuana uses, there is substantial evidence of its efficacy for a number of medical problems. A University of Vermont College of Medicine study indicates marijuana compounds increase cerebral blood flow, enhance cirtrial activity (brain), and kill respiratory pathogens, and provide inflammatory relief (arthritis).
